one_liner: Rust crate that hashes 2/4/8 equal-length inputs at once with SIMD Keccak-256; ~5.5x per hash over keccak-asm (README).
what_it_does: Computes Ethereum/Swarm-style Keccak-256 (legacy 0x01 padding) for many independent messages in one call: keccak256_many::<N>(&[&[u8]; N]) with a compile-time N >= 2, or keccak256_many_into(&[&[u8]], &mut [[u8; 32]]) for a runtime count. Every input in a call must have the same length (the call panics otherwise), and the batch is split greedily into 8/4/2/1-wide chunks for the widest backend the CPU has. It also ships a scalar one-shot keccak256() and a streaming Keccak256 hasher with the same shape as alloy's Keccak256 plus RustCrypto digest traits, but those single-message paths are not faster than tiny-keccak.
how_it_is_fast: It does not speed up a single Keccak-f[1600] permutation. It runs one independent state per SIMD lane: 8 states in AVX-512 zmm registers, 4 with AVX2, 2 with SSE2/NEON/wasm simd128. The permutation is written once, generic over a small Lane trait (xor, andnot, rotate, splat, load, store). The 25-lane state is passed by value and rho/pi is unrolled so LLVM can keep the lanes in vector registers. The maintainers' disassembly (PRs #7 and #15) shows the AVX-512 build already fuses chi/theta into vpternlogq and turns the rotates into immediate vprolq. Spilling from register pressure on the 25-lane state is the remaining bottleneck, and the gather/scatter transpose costs about 9%.
when_to_use: Merkle/BMT levels, proof systems or sampling loops that hash many independent 64-byte (one-permutation) inputs in Ethereum/Swarm Keccak-256
x86-64 servers with AVX-512F (8-wide, ~5.4x over the crate's scalar path at 64 B) or AVX2 (4-wide, ~3.1x at 64 B)
Bulk hashing of equal-length blocks up to multi-KiB (README reports ~4-5x at 4 KiB, 8-wide)
wasm with simd128 enabled at build time, where the 2-wide path took the 64-byte hash from ~379 ns to ~222 ns under wasmtime
Rust code already generic over digest::Digest or alloy's Keccak256 shape that also needs a batch entry point
when_not_to_use: Single-message or latency-bound hashing: keccak256/Keccak256 run the scalar path, which the README puts at parity with tiny-keccak and ~1.3x slower than keccak-asm
Inputs of mixed lengths: a batch absorbs in lockstep and panics on unequal lengths, so you must bucket inputs by length yourself
FIPS-202 SHA3-256, SHAKE or other Keccak widths: only legacy-padded Keccak-256 with a 32-byte output is implemented
Proprietary or closed-source products: AGPL-3.0-or-later copyleft, and there is no C/C++ API
aarch64 servers looking for more than 2-wide: aarch64 is fixed at NEON width 2, and there is no SVE path or use of the ARMv8.2 SHA3 instructions

integration.dependencies: digest 0.11 (optional, default-on feature 'digest'); otherwise none (std required: dispatch uses is_x86_feature_detected!, std::env and a std atomic)
integration.platforms: x86-64 (SSE2 baseline 2-wide; AVX2 4-wide; AVX-512F+AVX2 8-wide, runtime-detected), aarch64 (NEON 2-wide), wasm32 (2-wide only with +simd128 at compile time, else scalar), other targets scalar
integration.thread_safety: Not documented; the batch functions are pure and the only shared state is an atomic cache of the detected width, and Keccak256 is a plain owned value
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — keccak256()/Keccak256 match alloy's Keccak256 shape and digest traits, but they are scalar; the speedup needs the new equal-length batch API

gotchas: The detected width and the KECCAK_BATCH_NO_AVX512 / KECCAK_BATCH_NO_AVX2 caps are read once and cached per process, so set the env vars before the first hash
keccak256_many::<1> is a compile error, but keccak256_many_into accepts a count of 0 or 1 and runs the scalar path
The README numbers don't compose: ~5.4x over scalar divided by keccak-asm's ~1.3x over scalar gives ~4.2x, yet the README claims ~5.5x over keccak-asm
AVX-512 kernels require only avx512f (plus avx2 for batch tails); on parts where AVX-512 downclocks, the README suggests capping to AVX2
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over KangarooTwelve/XKCP when you must keep Ethereum/Swarm Keccak-256 output and want a native Rust crate. XKCP also ships parallel Keccak-p[1600] times2/times4 kernels, but in C. BLAKE3 or blake2_simd are faster choices only when you are free to change the hash function.
verified_claims_summary: The crate's own perf example, run with cargo --release on an unnamed 'Zen-class AVX-512 part', measured 8-wide batched Keccak-256 at ~5.4x (64 B) and ~4-5x (4 KiB) per hash over its scalar path; open PR #15 names the maintainer's Zen 4 host as a Ryzen 9 7940HS and puts width-8 at ~3.5 us per 64 hashes. The tiny-keccak parity and keccak-asm comparisons (~1.3x over scalar; batch ~5.5x over keccak-asm) come from an unpublished same-binary harness; the public examples/perf.rs and benches/keccak.rs time only the crate's own scalar vs batch.
status_note: Active but very young: created 2026-07-02, one crates.io release (0.1.0, ~3.2k downloads, single reverse dependency nectar-primitives), last main commit 2026-07-24, README still says pre-release. AGPL-3.0-or-later limits use to copyleft-compatible projects.
